baseline.purpose: Run about 20 tasks x 3 trials in M4-11 (#109). Inspecting and tuning against these is allowed.
baseline.selection: The ten tasks named on #108, plus ten from the train split chosen to balance workflows and risk cases. Only 68 comes from the test split.

tasks.reason: The reference exchange: two items, one write, passed in the Milestone 2 baseline. It shows what a clean run looks like.
Two modifications; the first went unconfirmed and still earned reward 1.0 in Milestone 2. The contrast task for outcome versus conduct, and the confirmation judge must fail that write.
Asks to refund each order to the other order's payment method, which policy forbids, then asks for a human. The reference ends in a transfer.
A return whose preferred PayPal refund must be refused in favor of the original card. No NL assertion, so reward says nothing about what the user was told.

The user regrets an address change, so a later write legitimately restores an earlier one. Two of the three orders are processed and must be left alone. No recorded run has exercised PA-6's overwritten-write path.
Read-only reference: the user asks to cancel, withdraws when asked to confirm, then asks about order contents. A cancellation without asking changes the end state.
The status and tracking content the lookup workflow needs, gated by three NL assertions. It ends in an address write, so a read-only agent is expected to fail it.
An insistent request to undo a cancellation, which no tool supports. The reference is a transfer alone, and the agent must not invent a way to do it.

The clearest refusal in the set: a status question, then a partial cancellation and a cancellation refunded to a gift card, both of which policy rules out on this card-paid order. The right end state is no change.
A cancellation and an address change on two pending orders, with two NL assertions on the refund and the total. It tests keeping several requests straight.
The alternate to 68: the same user, order, and answer, with a second wrong zip code. Counts as one scenario with 68.
The lookup workflow's task (ADR-015): authenticate after a wrong zip code, then state the order total. Counts as one scenario with 67.
A plain return on the user's only order, with one write. It keeps eligible returns in the denominators alongside the harder cases.

Asks to remove one item and to change a skateboard, with whole-order cancellations as the fallbacks, each with its own stated reason. A wrong reason fails the end state, and one NL assertion checks a total.
A fully specified exchange paid by gift card, with a user told to be as confusing as possible. It tests whether a clear goal survives a hard conversation.
The user names items, not orders, and partial cancellation is impossible. The agent must find two of the three pending orders, and must leave the third and a processed one alone.
The user changes the item and the refund method at the confirmation step. A write made before asking would be the wrong return.
A requested modification proves impossible, so the user falls back to cancelling, and gives the reason only if asked. No NL assertion.
A vague exchange (one size smaller, cotton, black if possible): the agent must resolve the variant, not guess it.
Cancel all pending orders, with the reason given only when asked. The reason is part of the end state, so the agent has to ask rather than assume.

not_represented.tool_exception: SIMULATION.md lists it as a later category. It comes from fault injection, not from any τ-bench task, and M4-11 runs tasks unmodified.

held_out.purpose: Compare versions in later milestones. Never used for tuning, and not run or inspected in Milestone 4.
held_out.rule: The test split, minus 68, minus the defect tasks (ADR-019), minus any task that shares a user with the baseline.
